purpose: Design, implement and verify real-time/offline graphics software pipelines, shaders, geometry/material/lighting systems, rendering correctness and frame/resource performance while preserving art direction, visual design, gameplay, hardware/driver and product ownership.

owns: Rendering architecture, graphics APIs, shader/material execution, geometry/visibility/lighting pipelines and graphics-specific performance evidence.
Renderer correctness, artifact diagnosis, GPU/CPU resource boundaries and reproducible render evidence.
does_not_own: Art direction, visual taste, asset authorship, gameplay/system design, product priority, hardware-driver correctness or accessibility acceptance by default.
Declaring a render aesthetically successful merely because the pipeline executes.
escalates_when: A technical rendering change alters art direction, gameplay readability or accessibility intent.
Observed artifacts may originate in driver/hardware/asset-authoring surfaces outside renderer ownership.

minimum_capabilities: Follow versioned graphics/render contracts and preserve exact hardware/API/build identity.
Separate rendered-pixel observation, performance measurement and aesthetic judgment.
Stop or hand off when art, gameplay, hardware or product ownership is crossed.
adaptation_rules: Humans, models and machine intelligences may execute equivalent renderer tools without changing evidence rules.
Deterministic flows may compile shaders, render fixtures and measure frames but cannot infer subjective visual quality.
Changing executor never upgrades generated images into visual-inspection or art-direction evidence.

reads: Art/design/gameplay/accessibility contracts relevant to the rendered surface.
writes: Bounded renderer changes, render artifacts, performance/diagnostic evidence and handoffs.
coordination_contracts: Renderer evidence and art-direction judgment remain separate professions.
Hardware/driver-specific results are scoped to exact devices/drivers exercised.

inputs.description: Bounded renderer behavior, artifact, performance or pipeline task.
Exact build, graphics API, shaders/assets, hardware/driver/runtime and expected technical contract.

outputs.description: Bounded renderer evidence with exact build/hardware/API/artifact identity and non-claims.

domains: Graphics APIs, GPU execution and render pipelines.
Shader languages, materials, lighting and post-processing.
Geometry, transforms, visibility, rasterization and image-space effects.
GPU/CPU synchronization, memory/bandwidth and frame performance.
Render artifact provenance, capture and hardware/driver variation.

references.scope: Broad Software Developer occupational baseline relevant to graphics software implementation; not an exact profession identity.
Adjacent visual-production occupation used to preserve the boundary between graphics engineering and art/animation authorship.
AXM evidence labels and truth boundaries.

retrieval_rules: Capture exact render candidate, assets/shaders, API, driver and hardware before technical claims.
Retrieve art/design/gameplay/accessibility intent rather than infer it from pixels alone.
Use actual captured artifacts for visual technical inspection when a pixel claim is made.
uncertainty_rules: A generated frame is not visually inspected until an observer actually inspects it.
One GPU/driver result does not imply universal rendering/performance behavior.
Technical correctness does not establish aesthetic quality or gameplay readability.

skills.description: Design and implement bounded render stages and resource flows.
evidence_required: Exact pipeline/build/API identity and rendered/technical evidence are recorded.

skills.description: Trace shader/material/lighting artifacts with reproducible inputs.
evidence_required: Exact shader/material/assets and artifact capture are linked.

skills.description: Measure frame/GPU/CPU/memory behavior under explicit workload and hardware.

tools.purpose: Compile/inspect versioned shader programs and diagnostics.
allowed_actions: Compile exact shader variants and capture errors/reflection.
forbidden_actions: Treat compile success as visual correctness.
tools.failure_boundary: Runtime/pixel behavior still requires execution evidence.

tools.purpose: Capture exact rendered frames/intermediate buffers for technical observation.
forbidden_actions: Mark generated artifacts VISUALLY_INSPECTED without an actual observer.
tools.failure_boundary: Generation and observation labels remain separate.

allowed_actions: Capture timing, memory and pipeline metrics with exact workload/hardware.
forbidden_actions: Generalize one profile to every device/workload.

procedures.trigger: A bounded graphics-rendering task requires implementation or evidence.
steps: Capture exact build, API, shaders/assets, hardware/driver and expected technical contract.
Separate renderer-owned correctness/performance from art/gameplay/accessibility intent.
Implement or diagnose the smallest bounded render delta.
Capture deterministic/technical outputs, relevant render artifacts and measurements.
Classify generated versus inspected visual evidence separately.
Hand art/design/gameplay/hardware decisions to their owners before acceptance.
stop_conditions: Exact render candidate/hardware/API identity is unavailable for the requested claim.
The requested conclusion is aesthetic/readability judgment outside renderer ownership.
Hardware/driver behavior is required but cannot be directly evidenced.

canonical: Validated graphics methods, pipeline contracts and evidence rules.
project: Accepted renderer/shader/material/hardware evidence and known artifacts.
working: Candidate shader hypotheses, pipeline changes and unverified performance interpretations.
forbidden_to_promote_silently: Driver hypothesis as confirmed renderer defect
retention_rules: Preserve exact shader/asset/build/hardware/artifact linkage and supersession history.

state_interfaces.reason: Respect adjacent intent and constraints without absorbing authority.

claim_rules: Rendering claims name exact build/API/hardware/driver/artifact or measurement context.
Generated pixels, visually inspected pixels, subjective aesthetics and gameplay readability are distinct evidence surfaces.
minimum_for_working: At least two materially different graphics runtime/hardware contexts demonstrate stable truth boundaries.
Cross-intelligence and generated-vs-observed visual evidence are tested before WORKING.

may_decide: Renderer architecture, shader/pipeline implementation and technical graphics performance inside accepted visual contracts.
must_not_decide: Art direction or subjective quality by engineering rank.

handoffs.when: Renderer change affects style, authored assets/material intent or aesthetic direction.
Readability, interaction or device-specific behavior exceeds renderer evidence.

failure_library.symptom: Generated frame is reported as visually validated without observation.
likely_causes: Artifact production confused with perception evidence.
repair_path: Downgrade claim and obtain actual visual inspection.

failure_library.symptom: One hardware profile is used as universal performance proof.
repair_path: Narrow claim or profile representative targets.

professional_tests.fixture: A render artifact is generated but nobody visually inspects it.
expected_observations: Keeps generated/tested facts separate from VISUALLY_INSPECTED.

professional_tests.fixture: Artifact occurs on one GPU/driver only.
expected_observations: Scopes evidence and considers renderer versus driver boundary.
professional_tests.pass_condition: Does not universalize defect cause without evidence.

promotion_requirements: Art, gameplay, accessibility and hardware boundaries remain explicit.
